clue.text: A choice of courses or delicacies

definitions.meaning: read as two separate words, sweet or meats, a pick between two parts of a dinner menu
sugary treats and confections, the usual sense

explanation.surface: A menu offering several courses or fancy treats.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words, each a course you might choose: pudding (a sweet) or a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Confectionery items such as candied fruit are dainty treats, i.e. delicacies; split in two, the word names a dessert course and a main course.

parts.note: the famous long fortification across northern China, a structure built up from stone and earth

explanation.surface: A big Chinese escalation of something, perhaps military.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great one in China is the best-known example of this kind of built structure, a barrier raised up course by course.

clue.text: Possibly run and see to make certain

indicators.note: something done possibly may be done some other way, so these letters are taken in another order

explanation.surface: Advice to go running and look around so that you can be sure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges RUN and SEE together; 'and' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to make certain of something is to guarantee it.

definitions.meaning: embalmed bodies from ancient Egypt, kept intact for millennia
an affectionate British word for mothers

explanation.surface: Egyptian mothers and fathers in good shape for their age.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum is British for mom, so the plural doubles as mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: Embalmed corpses wrapped in bandages from ancient Egypt, and also a homely British plural for mothers.

clue.text: A number given to someone to sing

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A song assigned to a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' just joins A, L (Roman fifty) and TO; the surface reads as a song handed to a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer with the voice range below soprano is someone who sings in a choir.

parts.note: someone who hatches a plot, a conspirator, rather than a novelist or a builder of a plot of land

explanation.surface: A novelist or a property builder working on a plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspirator who devises intrigues develops plots in the sense of secret plans.

parts.note: the stock phrase for alcohol read literally, as a wicked being that is also strong liquor

explanation.surface: The old phrase blaming alcohol for ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent ghost is a demon, and spirit is also a word for strong liquor, so the phrase is both.

parts.note: music used to rock a baby to sleep in its earliest days, not rock and roll

explanation.surface: A history of rock and roll's beginnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A lullaby sung while rocking an infant is a form of rocking music heard very early in life.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: Parcels have all been delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler's set of six deliveries is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketing set of six balls, and an adverb meaning finished.

clue.text: Draw stumps in an evenly contested game

definitions.text: Draw stumps in an evenly contested game

parts.words: Draw stumps in an evenly contested game
parts.note: in cricket, stumps are drawn at the end of play, a finish described by the first word of the answer, in a tight contest

explanation.surface: Play ends during a tight cricket game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'drawing stumps' marks the close of play; a tight, even contest is the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight, evenly balanced contest; the first word also names the end of a day's cricket.

clue.text: With a new clue I'd find the mathematician

indicators.note: making something new out of the letters means arranging them into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint that leads to a famous geometer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLUE to EUCL, then I'D follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Elements, the father of geometry, was a famous mathematician.

explanation.surface: Someone pulls out a funding instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A region that breaks away from a federation formally withdraws from it.

indicators.note: being on a ship puts a thing inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board means on a ship, SS, steamship

explanation.surface: Messages sent that make people laugh on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' means inside SS, the abbreviation for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dispatch is to kill, as a butcher kills animals.

clue.text: Legal document that could be a trap

definitions.meaning: a deed transferring property from one owner to another
a light horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle

explanation.surface: A contract that might ensnare the signer.
explanation.walkthrough: A trap here is a small two-wheeled horse-drawn cart, not a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed transferring title to land, and any vehicle for transport, such as a pony cart.

parts.note: an old golf club with a lofted face, made to hit the ball high

explanation.surface: An ambitious society.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned golf club with much loft, roughly a three-wood, sends the ball upward.

clue.text: Not a change for the better

definitions.text: Not a change for the better

parts.words: Not a change for the better
parts.note: a turn back to worse health after improving, so a change for the worse

explanation.surface: A complaint about a reform that failed.
explanation.definitionFit: A return to illness after recovery is a deterioration, the opposite of an improvement.

clue.text: It flies a welcome in the British fleet

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another

explanation.surface: A flag hoisted as a greeting among British warships.
explanation.walkthrough: AVE is a Latin greeting, here placed inside RN.
explanation.definitionFit: A large black bird of the crow family, something that flies.

indicators.note: a container holding something has it inside

explanation.surface: A crate containing an oriental arm.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance for throwing or thrusting is an example of a weapon.

parts.note: an, the indefinite article in its other form

indicators.note: a mirror shows a reflection, so the word is read back to front

explanation.surface: A woman writing a thoughtful piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflective' turns AN into NA; the result reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so a woman, referred to as she.

clue.text: Musical group get port after the end of the concert

indicators.note: the port comes after the other piece
the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Musicians head to a harbour once the concert finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Three performers together are a small musical ensemble.

clue.text: A capital ring from one's lover

explanation.surface: A ring received from one's beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shakespearean suitor of Juliet, whose name is used for any ardent male admirer.

clue.text: I write in red — not green

explanation.surface: A note about writing in red ink rather than green.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is no longer unripe has matured.

explanation.surface: Porridge being served at the morning table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats cooked in milk or water make porridge.

clue.text: Used in making her kind of pickle

indicators.note: the answer is used in the letters running across these words

explanation.surface: A recipe ingredient for a woman's favourite pickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cucumber preserved in vinegar is a type of pickle.

indicators.note: a type of the word is a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A coloured badge for identification.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge showing who someone is serves as an identifying label.

parts.note: an eye is the organ that views

explanation.surface: A spyhole for a prospective tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hole, as in fabric or a door, is a little opening one can peep through.

clue.text: Nectar may produce a state of ecstasy

indicators.note: producing a new word from these letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Drink of the gods brings rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamlike, rapt condition of mind, akin to ecstasy.

clue.text: Politician is about to see mischief-makers

indicators.note: the outer word goes about the inner

explanation.surface: An MP is about to meet troublemakers.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a British Member of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Small devils, or naughty children, cause mischief.

parts.note: read as the clipped form of the long word for bullets and shells

explanation.surface: Running low on bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal clipped form of the word for bullets and shells.

parts.note: a French term for a pen name, of which Anatole France, the writer's adopted name, is an instance

explanation.surface: A geography lesson naming France as a French-speaking example.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France was the pseudonym of the French novelist Jacques Thibault.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseudonym used by an author; Anatole France is a famous instance.

definitions.meaning: a frame for holding things, like a plate stand
to inflict severe pain on, as on the medieval instrument

explanation.surface: Endure being tortured.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework for storing items, and to torment someone severely.

clue.text: To lead on is wrong, causing great distress

indicators.note: putting the letters wrong means setting them out of order

explanation.surface: Deceiving someone is wrong and causes misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate grief or misery is a state of great distress.
